requirements.verifier_assertion: For every enumeration/traversal/filter case in CASES, TREE_CASES, path_sum variants, left_view/right_view, flatten, and bit_manipulation.subsets, the API's return value must NOT be an instance of list/tuple/set/frozenset/dict/str; the assertion is `not isinstance(result, (list, tuple, set, frozenset, dict, str))`.

For every enumeration/traversal/filter case above, `iter(result) is result` — i.e. the returned object is its own iterator (single-pass), not an iterable that produces a fresh iterator on each `iter()` call.
After a full pass (`list(result)`), a second `list(result)` must return [] — the single-pass iterator is exhausted, not restartable.
must_include: after a full pass it must be exhausted

requirements.verifier_assertion: For every case in CASES, TREE_CASES, path_sum variants, view functions, flatten, and bit_manipulation.subsets, the materialized list of items must equal (or match as a multiset if `order_matters=False`) the frozen pre-change golden output in tests/golden.json.

The verifier imports and calls `permute_iter`, `palindromic_substrings_iter`, `flatten_iter`, `get_factors_iterative1`, `get_factors_iterative2` — these `*_iter`-named legacy symbols must remain importable from their prior modules and callable with their prior signatures.

`inorder_rec(tree, acc)`, `preorder_rec(tree, acc)`, `postorder_rec(tree, acc)`, and `flatten([1, [2, [3]]], acc)` must accept the accumulator-list positional argument without raising; the accumulator gets filled with the traversal / flatten result, and the return may still be a list.

`fizzbuzz(0)` and `fizzbuzz(-2)` raise ValueError immediately at the call site (not wrapped inside `list(...)`); both `max_sliding_window` implementations raise ValueError immediately at the call site for `k <= 0`. The verifier uses `with pytest.raises(ValueError):` around the plain call.

For both `algorithms.heap.sliding_window_max.max_sliding_window` and `algorithms.queue.max_sliding_window.max_sliding_window`, when `k == len(nums)`, `list(fn(nums, len(nums))) == [max(nums)]` (exactly one full window). The k-greater-than-length result is the singleton maximum, interpreted under the lazy iterator return contract.
For both variants above, when `k > len(nums)`, `list(fn(nums, len(nums)+1)) == []` — no complete window fits.
For both variants above, `list(fn([], 3)) == []` — an empty input produces zero windows.

For both variants above, `fn(nums, 0)` and `fn(nums, -3)` raise ValueError EAGERLY at the moment of the call (verifier uses `with pytest.raises(ValueError):` around the plain call, not around `list(...)`).
Both `algorithms.heap.sliding_window_max` and `algorithms.queue.max_sliding_window` are imported and asserted-against by the verifier; the unified semantics must hold for BOTH modules, not just one.

`merge_sort`, `quick_sort`, `merge_intervals`, `top_1`, `find_all_cliques`, `k_closest`, `group_anagrams`, `top_view`, and `bottom_view` continue to return `list` (checked via `isinstance(result, list)`); the refactor must not over-convert these to iterators.

For the tree-view family: `left_view` and `right_view` are asserted lazy (return single-pass iterator, empty for `None` input); `top_view` and `bottom_view` are asserted to return `list` (stay materialized). The refactor must distinguish these four APIs, not treat views as one class.

For `permute(range(11))`, `generate_parenthesis_v1(15)`, `subsets(range(24))`, `gen_strobogrammatic(20)`, `letter_combinations('9'*12)`, the first item must be produced within 15 seconds inside a subprocess (30s hard kill). An `iter(eager_list)` implementation cannot pass this bar because the eager list build itself already blows past the budget for these input sizes.
must_include: producing the first item does not require
